context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:2243-2277 (tryRemoteCompaction) builds the prompt directly from `ctx` via PromptAssembly.build(...) and calls `model.compactConversationHistory(prompt, settings)` with no preceding trim. context-compaction.description: When the active history's estimated tokens exceed the FULL model context window (not merely the auto-compact limit), upstream trims trailing tool-output/developer items before issuing the remote compact request so the request fits. Swift sends the untrimmed history. Per upstream contract a remote compact request failure is terminal (compact_remote.rs:128-135 emits Error and returns Err), so in this edge case Swift's remote compaction request fails where upstream would have trimmed and succeeded. context-compaction.fixRecommendation: Add a `trimToFitContextWindow` step in SessionEngine.tryRemoteCompaction before building the prompt: while `ctx.estimatedTokens > modelContextWindow(modelOverride:)`, if the last history item is codex-generated (tool output / developer/context message) call `ctx.removeLastItem()`, else break. Mirror compact_remote.rs:361-388 (is_codex_generated_item + remove_last_item, stop when not codex-generated or estimate fits).

model-client.title: response.function_call_arguments.delta is surfaced as ToolCallInputDelta but upstream ignores it
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:280-289 — process_responses_event has a branch ONLY for "response.custom_tool_call_input.delta"; there is NO branch for "response.function_call_arguments.delta", so it falls into the `_ =>` arm (responses.rs:391-393) and yields nothing. The test `parses_tool_call_input_deltas` (responses.rs:765-795) sends a `response.function_call_arguments.delta` frame and asserts events has only 2 entries (events[1] is Completed), proving the function_call_arguments.delta produces NO ResponseEvent. A repo-wide grep confirms no other handler exists outside test modules.
model-client.swiftStatus: OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:720-734, URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:463-475, WebSocketResponsesClient.swift:311-324 all group `"response.function_call_arguments.delta"` together with `"response.custom_tool_call_input.delta"` and emit `.toolCallInputDelta`. The SessionEngine treats `.toolCallInputDelta` as a no-op (SessionEngine.swift:2921-2929), so today it is harmless, but the ResponseEvent stream contract diverges: Swift emits an event upstream guarantees not to emit.
model-client.description: Upstream intentionally does not translate streaming function-call argument deltas into a ResponseEvent (the full arguments arrive via response.output_item.done); the Swift port emits an extra ToolCallInputDelta per function_call_arguments.delta frame across all three transports. A frontend or future consumer that accumulates tool-call argument deltas would double-count (deltas + final arguments) on the Swift port but not upstream.
model-client.fixRecommendation: Remove `"response.function_call_arguments.delta"` from the combined case in OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:720, URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:463, and WebSocketResponsesClient.swift:311, leaving only `"response.custom_tool_call_input.delta"`. Let function_call_arguments.delta fall through to the default/no-op arm to match upstream.

model-client.title: WebSocket create event strips the `stream` field that upstream keeps
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-api/src/common.rs:216-240 — ResponseCreateWsRequest has `pub stream: bool` with NO skip_serializing_if, and `From<&ResponsesApiRequest>` (common.rs:192-213) copies `stream: request.stream`. The enum is serialized with `#[serde(tag="type")]` (common.rs:269-277) into `{"type":"response.create", ..., "stream":true, ...}`. So the upstream WS create payload always carries `"stream": true`.
model-client.swiftStatus: WebSocketResponsesClient.swift:146-152 — websocketCreateEvent() does `event.removeValue(forKey: "stream")` (and `background`). The base body from OpenAIResponsesClient.buildRequestBody sets `"stream": true` (OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:225), so the WS path emits a create event with no `stream` key, unlike upstream.
model-client.description: The Swift WebSocket transport removes the `stream` field from the response.create payload; upstream includes `stream: true`. The OpenAI WS endpoint likely tolerates the omission, but the request shape diverges from upstream for both the normal create and the generate=false prewarm.
model-client.fixRecommendation: In WebSocketResponsesClient.swift:149 do not remove `stream`; keep `event["stream"]` as-is (removing only `background`, which upstream never sets anyway), so the WS create/prewarm payload matches upstream's ResponseCreateWsRequest.

model-client.title: Tool-input delta dropped on empty delta string; upstream emits it
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:280-289 — the custom_tool_call_input.delta branch matches `if let (Some(delta), Some(item_id))`. In Rust `Some("")` is still `Some`, so an empty-string delta with a valid item_id DOES emit ResponseEvent::ToolCallInputDelta. Contrast with output_text.delta (responses.rs:275-279) which also emits on empty delta — both branches only test presence, not non-emptiness.
model-client.swiftStatus: OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:731 (`if let itemId, !d.isEmpty`), URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:472 (`if let itemId, !delta.isEmpty`), WebSocketResponsesClient.swift:321 (`if !suppressEvents, let itemId, !d.isEmpty`) all add a `!delta.isEmpty` guard, suppressing empty-delta tool-input frames. The adjacent comments claim 'only emits when BOTH a delta and a (resolved) id are present', misreading Rust's Option semantics where Some("") is present.
model-client.description: An empty-string tool-call-input delta with a valid id is emitted upstream but dropped by all three Swift transports due to the extra non-empty guard. Inconsistent with the Swift's own output_text/reasoning delta paths, which correctly emit empty deltas.
model-client.fixRecommendation: Remove the `!delta.isEmpty` / `!d.isEmpty` condition from the tool-input branches (OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:731, URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:472, WebSocketResponsesClient.swift:321); guard only on a resolved itemId, matching upstream's `Some(delta)` presence test.

model-client.title: WebSocket response.completed accepts a missing `id` where upstream treats it as fatal
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:358-374 — response.completed deserializes `response` into ResponseCompleted{ id: String (required) } and on failure returns Err(ApiError::Stream("failed to parse ResponseCompleted: …")). responses_websocket.rs:9-10,745 confirms the WS path uses the SAME process_responses_event, so a missing id is fatal on WS too.
model-client.swiftStatus: WebSocketResponsesClient.swift:411-413 — `let id = resp?["id"] as? String ?? "resp"` silently substitutes a synthetic id and yields .completed. The HTTP/URLSession path correctly errors on missing id (URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:564-572), so the two Swift transports diverge from each other and the WS one from upstream.
model-client.description: On the WebSocket transport, a malformed response.completed frame without `id` is treated as a successful completion with id "resp" rather than the fatal stream-parse error upstream produces. Real servers always send id, so low traffic, but it is a transport-fidelity gap and an intra-Swift inconsistency.
model-client.fixRecommendation: In WebSocketResponsesClient.swift, for genuine response.completed frames (not the max_output_tokens incomplete fallthrough) finish with a retryable ModelError when `id` is absent, mirroring URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:564-572.

model-client.title: Retry backoff uses AWS full-jitter instead of upstream's 200ms*2^(n-1)*[0.9,1.1] and clamps retry-after
model-client.rustEvidence: core/src/util.rs:8-9,85-89 — backoff(attempt) = INITIAL_DELAY_MS(200) * 2^(attempt-1) * rand(0.9..1.1); no max cap. session/turn.rs:1123-1128 — the retry delay is `requested_delay.unwrap_or_else(|| backoff(retries))`, i.e. a server-provided retry-after (Stream requested_delay) is used DIRECTLY with no clamping.
model-client.swiftStatus: InfraPrimitives/Backoff.swift:3-19 — full-jitter: delay = random(0, min(maxDelay, base*2^attempt)). RetryingModelClient.swift:40-46 clamps retry-after to maxRetryDelay (`min(retryAfter.seconds, maxRetryDelay.seconds)`, default 20s) before sleeping; upstream applies no such cap.
model-client.description: Two timing divergences: (a) jitter distribution differs — upstream multiplies the exponential by a narrow 0.9–1.1 factor and has no upper cap, while Swift uses unbounded-style full jitter capped at retryMaxDelay; (b) Swift clamps an SSE-provided retry-after to 20s whereas upstream honors the full server-requested delay. Behavioral (timing) only, no wire effect, but deviates from upstream's documented backoff contract.
model-client.fixRecommendation: If exact retry timing parity matters, replace the full-jitter Backoff for the model-client retry path with `200ms * 2^(attempt-1) * random(0.9..1.1)` and stop clamping retryAfter to maxRetryDelay in RetryingModelClient.swift:40-43 (use the server-provided delay directly).

model-client.title: Header-derived ServerModel seeds last_server_model, suppressing a duplicate in-stream emission upstream would send
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:41-67 emits the header openai-model as ServerModel during spawn but process_sse starts with `last_server_model: None` (responses.rs:407). So if an in-stream response.headers carries the SAME model as the response header, upstream emits ServerModel a second time (last_server_model was None at loop start).
model-client.swiftStatus: URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:236 sets `lastServerModel = model` from the header value before the stream loop, so an in-stream frame repeating that model is deduped and NOT re-emitted, unlike upstream.
model-client.description: The Swift seeds the per-event dedup state from the header ServerModel, which can suppress a duplicate ServerModel event that upstream would emit when the first in-stream headers frame repeats the header model. Edge case / low traffic, observable only by a consumer counting ServerModel events.
model-client.fixRecommendation: In URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:236, emit the header-derived ServerModel without assigning it to `lastServerModel` (leave lastServerModel nil at loop start) to match upstream's independent header-vs-stream emission, if exact event-count parity is desired.

tools-router.title: MCP tool calls advertised parallel-safe; upstream always serializes them
tools-router.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/handlers/mcp.rs:86-88 `fn supports_parallel_tool_calls(&self) -> bool { self.tool_info.supports_parallel_tool_calls }`; the production value is set in codex-mcp/src/rmcp_client.rs:378 `supports_parallel_tool_calls: false` (and mcp/mod.rs:446 also false). So every MCP tool is SERIAL upstream — it takes the exclusive side of the per-turn tool gate (tools/parallel.rs).

ToolRouter.dispatch then takes gate.acquireRead() for it, allowing concurrent execution with other parallel-safe tools.
tools-router.description: Upstream runs MCP tool calls serially (exclusive gate); the Swift port runs them in parallel (shared gate). This changes intra-turn concurrency/ordering: an MCP call can race with other reads in Swift but is fully serialized upstream. Affects any client whose MCP server has ordering/side-effect assumptions.
tools-router.fixRecommendation: In Sources/MCP/McpManager.swift change McpToolProxy.parallelSafe to false (or thread the per-tool advertised value through, but upstream's rmcp client always sends false, so a constant false is the faithful reproduction).

tools-router.title: MCP resource tools advertised parallel-safe; upstream are serial (default)
tools-router.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/handlers/mcp_resource.rs has NO supports_parallel_tool_calls override, so ListMcpResourcesHandler / ListMcpResourceTemplatesHandler / ReadMcpResourceHandler inherit the default `false` (tools/src/tool_executor.rs:49-51 `fn supports_parallel_tool_calls -> false`).
tools-router.swiftStatus: Sources/MCP/McpResourceTools.swift:59, 121, 185 all declare `public let parallelSafe = true` for list_mcp_resources, list_mcp_resource_templates, read_mcp_resource.
tools-router.description: The three MCP resource tools are serial upstream but parallel-safe in Swift. They are read-only listing/read operations so the practical impact is low, but the gating diverges from upstream.
tools-router.fixRecommendation: Set parallelSafe = false on ListMcpResourcesTool, ListMcpResourceTemplatesTool, and ReadMcpResourceTool in Sources/MCP/McpResourceTools.swift to match the default serial gating.

tools-router.title: Tool-definition JSON inner field order diverges from upstream (sortedKeys reorders schema fields)
tools-router.rustEvidence: tools/src/json_schema.rs:33-55 declares JsonSchema with serde field order type, description, enum, items, properties, required, additionalProperties, anyOf; tools/src/tool_spec.rs:79-89 serializes each ToolSpec via serde_json::to_value preserving struct field order, so a string property serializes as {"type":"string","description":...}. The properties BTreeMap (json_schema.rs:45) keeps keys alphabetical.
tools-router.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:251-252 parses each spec.parametersJSON into [String:Any]; line 382/439 then serializes the whole body with JSONSerialization options [.sortedKeys]. Verified empirically that .sortedKeys reorders nested schema objects to {"description":...,"type":"string"} (alphabetical), i.e. description BEFORE type — the opposite of upstream's type-first serde order.
tools-router.description: Because the request body is emitted with .sortedKeys, every inner JsonSchema object's keys are alphabetized (additionalProperties/description/enum/... /type) rather than serde struct order (type first). Top-level property-name ordering matches upstream (both alphabetical), but the per-field ordering inside each property object differs, making the tool-definition bytes non-identical to upstream and reducing OpenAI prompt-cache hit parity. Output is deterministic (so no run-to-run drift), only cross-implementation byte-exactness is lost.
tools-router.fixRecommendation: If byte-exact tool-definition parity with upstream is required for prompt caching, build the tools array as a type that preserves serde-equivalent field order (type, description, enum, items, properties, required, additionalProperties, anyOf) and serialize without .sortedKeys for the tools subtree, or emit the tool JSON strings verbatim (they are already authored in upstream order) instead of round-tripping through [String:Any] + sortedKeys.

apply-patch.title: fileChange Update diff uses context radius 3 instead of upstream's 1
apply-patch.rustEvidence: apply-patch/src/lib.rs:820-827 `unified_diff_from_chunks` delegates to `unified_diff_from_chunks_with_context(..., /*context*/ 1, ...)`; lib.rs:840-841 `TextDiff::from_lines(...).unified_diff().context_radius(context)`. This `unified_diff` is stored on `protocol::FileChange::Update.unified_diff` (invocation.rs:207-224, verify_apply_patch_args). app-server-protocol/src/protocol/item_builders.rs:302-315 `format_file_change_diff` copies that `unified_diff` verbatim (plus a `\n\nMoved to: {path}` suffix for renames) into `FileUpdateChange.diff`, which is what the frontend renders. Net: Update diffs in the fileChange item have 1 line of surrounding context.
apply-patch.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/TurnDiffTracker.swift:76-88 `toFileUpdateChanges()` builds the Update `diff` via `ApplyPatch.makeUnifiedDiff(old:new:path:movePath:kind:.update)`, which routes through `ApplyPatch.diffBody` where Sources/Tools/ApplyPatch.swift:1002 hardcodes `let context = 3`. The result feeds the `item/fileChange/patchUpdated` notification (Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:3033-3036) and the final fileChange item (SessionEngine.swift:3273-3276). So Update diffs carry 3 context lines, not 1.
apply-patch.description: Upstream computes the per-file Update unified diff with similar's context_radius(1) (one context line above/below each change hunk). The Swift port reuses its general-purpose makeUnifiedDiff/diffBody, which is fixed at context=3. For any Update with surrounding unchanged lines, the `diff` string in the fileChange thread item and the item/fileChange/patchUpdated notification will contain up to 2 extra context lines per side and differently sized/positioned @@ hunk headers than upstream, so a frontend that renders or diffs against this field sees a different payload. (Add/Delete diffs are raw content and match; the separate turn/diff/updated Git diff at TurnDiffTracker.swift:267,312 correctly uses context 3 to match similar's DEFAULT and is NOT affected.)
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Make the context radius parameterizable in ApplyPatch.diffBody/makeUnifiedDiff (e.g. add a `context:` argument defaulting to 3) and have TurnDiffTracker.toFileUpdateChanges() (Sources/Tools/TurnDiffTracker.swift:77) pass context: 1 so the emitted FileUpdateChange.diff matches upstream `unified_diff_from_chunks`'s context_radius(1). Leave the turn/diff/updated path (TurnDiffTracker.swift:312) at context 3.

config.title: Profile-v2 name is not validated, allowing path traversal and invalid names
config.rustEvidence: protocol/src/config_types.rs:110-126 — `impl FromStr for ProfileV2Name` rejects empty names and any name containing a byte other than ASCII-alphanumeric/`_`/`-` (tests at :758-766 cover `"../foo"` and `""`). The loader only ever receives an already-validated `Option<ProfileV2Name>` (state.rs:39 `user_config_profile: Option<ProfileV2Name>`; loader/mod.rs:124,251), and core/src/config/mod.rs:1420-1428 builds the path as `format!("{profile_name}{CONFIG_PROFILE_V2_SUFFIX}")` from that validated value.
config.swiftStatus: Sources/Config/Config.swift:1140-1163 — `resolveProfileV2` returns the raw override/env String with no validation; `loadProfileV2Layer` only checks `!name.isEmpty` then calls `profileV2Path(name)` (:538-540) = `codexHome + "/" + name + ".config.toml"`. No alphanumeric/`_`/`-` check, so a name like `../../etc/cron.d/x` (or `../other`) escapes `$CODEX_HOME`. profileV2 originates from a CLI flag/env (codexd/main.swift:424 `configOverrides["profileV2"]`, codex-session/main.swift:100 `CODEX_PROFILE_V2`).
config.description: Upstream encodes profile-v2 names in a newtype whose only constructor (`FromStr`) enforces a strict character set and non-emptiness; an invalid name is a hard parse error surfaced to the user, and a traversal name can never reach the path builder. The Swift port carries the name as a plain String through `resolveProfileV2` -> `profileV2Path` with no equivalent validation, so an invalid or traversal name is silently accepted and used to construct the profile file path, diverging from upstream's behavior and removing the traversal guard.
config.fixRecommendation: In Sources/Config/Config.swift add a `ProfileV2Name`-equivalent validation (e.g. a static `validateProfileV2Name(_:) -> Bool` requiring non-empty and every Unicode scalar in [A-Za-z0-9_-]) and apply it in `resolveProfileV2`/`loadProfileV2Layer`: reject (return nil and/or set `loadError` with upstream's message `invalid --profile-v2 value `<value>`; pass a plain name such as `work``) when the name fails validation, before building `profileV2Path`.

The Swift port performs no such validation, so a malformed comma-separated value is silently accepted and surfaced verbatim, diverging from upstream's load-time error.

mcp.title: Configured bearer_token_env_var that is unset/empty silently connects unauthenticated instead of failing startup
mcp.rustEvidence: rmcp-client/src/rmcp_client.rs:421-446 resolve_bearer_token: when bearer_token_env_var is set in config but the env var is NotPresent it returns Err("Environment variable {env_var} for MCP server '{server_name}' is not set"), and empty value → Err("...is empty"). make_rmcp_client (rmcp_client.rs:635-639) propagates this as a hard StartupOutcomeError, so the server fails to start.
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/MCP/McpHttpClient.swift:145-154 authorizationHeader: when config.bearerTokenEnvVar is set but env[v] is nil or empty it falls through (no error), then tries OAuth, then returns nil → the request is sent with NO Authorization header. There is no startup-time validation that the named bearer-token env var exists and is non-empty.
mcp.description: Upstream treats a declared-but-unresolvable bearer_token_env_var as a fatal misconfiguration and refuses to start the server (preventing an accidental unauthenticated connection and surfacing a precise diagnostic). The Swift port silently degrades to an unauthenticated request, so a server the operator believes is protected by a bearer token will be contacted without one when the env var is missing/empty.
mcp.fixRecommendation: In McpHttpClient.initialize() (or McpManager.startAll before initialize), when config.bearerTokenEnvVar is non-nil, resolve it eagerly: if the env var is absent throw McpError with "Environment variable <var> for MCP server '<name>' is not set"; if present but empty throw "...is empty". Mirror resolve_bearer_token's three branches so a misconfigured server fails fast rather than connecting anonymously.

mcp.title: Direct mcpServer/tool/call path does not re-enforce the per-server enabled/disabled tool filter
mcp.rustEvidence: codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs:582-594 call_tool checks `if !client.tool_filter.allows(tool)` and returns Err("tool '{tool}' is disabled for MCP server '{server}'") before dispatching, regardless of how the call arrived.
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/MCP/McpManager.swift:566-574 callTool dispatches directly to the client with no enabled_tools/disabled_tools check; filtering is applied only at registration time (McpManager.startAll:479 via cfg.filterTools), so a frontend-issued mcpServer/tool/call (RequestRouter.swift:4752) can invoke a tool that was filtered out of model exposure.

mcp.fixRecommendation: Thread the per-server ToolFilter (enabled_tools/disabled_tools from McpServerConfig) into McpManager.callTool and reject disallowed tools with McpError.server("tool '<tool>' is disabled for MCP server '<server>'") before invoking client.callTool, matching connection_manager.call_tool.

hooks.title: PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PermissionRequest matcher aliases not honored (apply_patch -> Write/Edit)
hooks.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/hook_names.rs:34-39 HookToolName::apply_patch() sets matcher_aliases = ["Write","Edit"]; hooks/src/events/common.rs:137-146 matcher_inputs() returns the canonical name PLUS every alias; hooks/src/engine/dispatcher.rs:57-60 selects a handler if `matcher_inputs.iter().any(|input| matches_matcher(handler.matcher, Some(input)))`. So a PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PermissionRequest hook configured with matcher "Write" or "Edit" fires on apply_patch tool calls. core/src/hook_runtime.rs:159-160,219-220 thread matcher_aliases into every PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PermissionRequest request.
hooks.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Hooks.swift:455-466 HookRequest.matchString returns only `toolName ?? ""` (a single string); HookEngine.matches (Hooks.swift:1028-1042) / matchesMatcher (1050-1068) test the matcher against that one value. HookRequest has no matcher-aliases field and the SessionEngine fire sites (SessionEngine.swift:4185-4193 runPreToolHook, 4255-4266 firePermissionRequestHook, 4290-4299 firePostToolHook) pass only `toolName: name`. For apply_patch the passed name is the canonical "apply_patch" (confirmed by SessionEngine.swift:885-887 special-casing name=="apply_patch"), never "Write"/"Edit". A grep for matcherAliases/matcher_aliases across Sources/ returns nothing.
hooks.description: Upstream matches a tool-scoped hook (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest) when its matcher matches the canonical tool name OR any compatibility alias. The only aliases in use map apply_patch to the Claude-Code-style names Write and Edit. Swift only ever tests the matcher against the single canonical tool name, so a hook configured with matcher "Write" or "Edit" (a documented compatibility convention) will silently never fire on apply_patch tool calls, while upstream would run it. This changes which hooks execute (security/policy hooks could be silently skipped).
hooks.fixRecommendation: Add a `matcherAliases: [String]` field to HookRequest (Hooks.swift) defaulting to []. In HookEngine.matches, for .preToolUse/.permissionRequest/.postToolUse test the matcher against the full input set [matchString] + matcherAliases and return true if ANY matches (mirroring dispatcher.rs:57-60 + matcher_inputs). In SessionEngine.swift runPreToolHook/firePermissionRequestHook/firePostToolHook, pass matcherAliases = name == "apply_patch" ? ["Write","Edit"] : [] so apply_patch tool calls also select Write/Edit-matched hooks. Keep tool_name on stdin as the canonical name (already correct).

auth.title: account/rateLimits/read leaks raw backend plan_type instead of normalizing to PlanType wire enum

protocol-wire-types.title: serviceTier double-option three-state semantics collapsed to plain optional
protocol-wire-types.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs:99-106 (ThreadStartParams.service_tier) and v2/turn.rs:96-103 (TurnStartParams.service_tier): `pub service_tier: Option<Option<String>>` with custom `deserialize_double_option`/`serialize_double_option` + `skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none`. The outer Option distinguishes field-absent (inherit) from inner `None` (explicit `null` = clear/override to no service tier) from `Some(v)`.
protocol-wire-types.swiftStatus: Sources/ProtocolModel/ClientRequest.swift:124 (ThreadStartParams), :143 (ThreadResumeParams), :274 (TurnStartParams) and Sources/ProtocolModel/V2.swift:163: `public var serviceTier: String?` using default synthesized Codable. Swift's plain `String?` cannot distinguish absent-vs-null on decode and never emits an explicit `null` on encode, so the explicit-clear signal is lost. exec-unified-shell.title: Pre-spawn sandbox denial returns plain text instead of structured ExecCommandToolOutput

exec-unified-shell.title: Missing 100ms post-write reaction delay before reading in write_stdin
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs:621-626: after a successful non-empty `process.write(...)`, upstream does `tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await` to give the child a window to react so its output is captured in the following poll.
exec-unified-shell.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/UnifiedExec.swift:629-630: UnifiedExecManager.writeStdin calls `proc.writeStdin(input)` then immediately `proc.readWindow(...)` with no post-write sleep.
exec-unified-shell.description: Upstream inserts a fixed 100ms settle after writing stdin so a quick child echo/prompt lands inside the same read window. Swift omits it; the yield window still eventually captures output, but very short yield_time_ms calls may return before the child reacts, producing an empty output chunk that differs from upstream.
exec-unified-shell.fixRecommendation: In UnifiedExecManager.writeStdin, after a successful non-empty write add a ~100ms sleep (e.g. `try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 100_000_000)`) before readWindow, matching process_manager.rs:625.

exec-unified-shell.title: effective_max_output_tokens does not apply the turn truncation-policy token budget cap
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec.rs:75-80: `effective_max_output_tokens` = `resolve_max_tokens(max_output_tokens).min(truncation_policy.token_budget())` — the model-requested/default token cap is additionally clamped down to the turn's truncation budget.
exec-unified-shell.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/UnifiedExec.swift:1189-1192 / 775-778: maxBytes = min(maxOutputBytes, min(maxOutputTokens*4 or DEFAULT*4, UNIFIED_EXEC_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES)). There is no `.min(truncation_policy.token_budget())` term; the turn truncation policy is not plumbed into the exec tool.
exec-unified-shell.description: Upstream caps the returned token count by both resolve_max_tokens AND the active TruncationPolicy budget; Swift caps only by the static UNIFIED_EXEC_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES / harness maxToolOutputBytes. When a turn sets a tighter truncation budget, Swift can return more output tokens than upstream would.
exec-unified-shell.fixRecommendation: Plumb the turn truncation policy's token_budget() into ExecCommandTool/WriteStdinTool and clamp the resolved token cap with it, mirroring unified_exec.rs:79.

persistence-rollout.title: Rollout filename and date-partition directory computed in UTC instead of upstream's local time
persistence-rollout.rustEvidence: codex-rs/rollout/src/recorder.rs:1325-1346 precompute_log_file_info uses `OffsetDateTime::now_local()` for both the `sessions/<year>/<MM>/<DD>` directory (lines 1334-1336) and the `rollout-<date_str>-<uuid>.jsonl` filename timestamp (format `[year]-[month]-[day]T[hour]-[minute]-[second]`, lines 1340-1346). Note the in-line session_meta.timestamp is separately UTC (recorder.rs:1200-1203 `to_offset(UtcOffset::UTC)`).
persistence-rollout.swiftStatus: Sources/Persistence/ThreadStore.swift:111-121 rolloutPath() calls gmtime_r (UTC) for both the dateDir `%04d/%02d/%02d` and the filename `stamp` `%04d-%02d-%02dT%02d-%02d-%02d`. The comment claims parity with upstream layout but uses UTC, not local time.
persistence-rollout.description: Upstream partitions session files into sessions/YYYY/MM/DD and names the file using LOCAL wall-clock time; Swift uses UTC. For the same instant near local midnight (or any non-UTC timezone) a Swift-written rollout lands in a different YYYY/MM/DD folder and carries a different hh-mm-ss in its filename than upstream would for the same session. Both implementations parse the date back out of the filename consistently within themselves, and the cross-tool source-of-truth timestamp (session_meta.timestamp) is UTC on both sides, so this does not corrupt data — but a user inspecting ~/.codex/sessions in a non-UTC timezone sees Swift files in 'tomorrow's' (or yesterday's) date folder relative to CLI-written files, and date-bucketed listing/scan ordering can disagree at the day boundary.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: In ThreadStore.swift rolloutPath(), replace gmtime_r with localtime_r so the date-partition directory and filename timestamp use local wall-clock time, matching upstream OffsetDateTime::now_local(). Keep the session_meta.timestamp field on UTC (Rollout.swift rustTimestamp via gmtime_r) since upstream that field is UTC.

persistence-rollout.title: turn_aborted rollout event carries a non-upstream `error_info` field
persistence-rollout.rustEvidence: codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs:3692-3703 TurnAbortedEvent has only `turn_id: Option<String>`, `reason: TurnAbortReason`, `completed_at: Option<i64>`, `duration_ms: Option<i64>`. There is no `error_info` field on the event.
persistence-rollout.swiftStatus: Sources/Persistence/Rollout.swift:668-683 rustRolloutLine emits `payload["error_info"] = ei` on both the .interrupted and .failed turn_aborted event_msg lines, in addition to type/turn_id/reason.
persistence-rollout.description: The Swift writer adds an `error_info` key to the turn_aborted event_msg payload to preserve the fine-grained internal cause (StreamError, HookBlocked, etc.) after collapsing `reason` to one of upstream's 4 canonical TurnAbortReason strings. Upstream TurnAbortedEvent has no such field. Because the upstream struct is not `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, serde silently ignores the extra key on read, so this does NOT break upstream's load_rollout_items / RolloutLine parse — it is a tolerated extra field. Flagged only as a documented byte-level divergence from the upstream wire shape.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: Acceptable as-is given serde tolerance; if exact byte parity is desired, drop error_info from the turn_aborted payload and instead carry the cause in a separate native ({"t":...}) sidecar record that upstream readers ignore. No correctness fix required.
